line_offer_intro: Our recommendation for your offer, from the comparable sales, the market and this home's history. These three numbers are a negotiating plan, not a value opinion, so we'll adjust them together if anything changes.
line_credit_alt: Alternative: offer {price} and ask for {credit} toward your closing costs. Price minus credit is the same as {equiv} flat (the seller's percentage costs rise slightly with the price), and you'd need about {saved} less cash at closing than at {base} with no credit (less than the credit, since the higher price raises the down payment and closing costs). See Price vs. Seller Credit in the cost section.
line_credit_alt_no_saving: Alternative: offer {price} and ask for {credit} toward your closing costs. Price minus credit is the same as {equiv} flat (the seller's percentage costs rise slightly with the price), but the higher down payment and closing costs use up the credit, so it doesn't lower your cash at closing. See Price vs. Seller Credit in the cost section.

line_buydown: Or use the credit to lower your payment instead. A {credit} credit put toward a temporary 2-1 rate buydown at {price} (which costs about {cost}) would make your payment about {y1} in year one and {y2} in year two, then {full} after that. That trades cash-at-closing help for two years of lower payments.
line_buydown_short: Or use the credit to lower your payment instead. A 2-1 rate buydown at {price} would cost about {cost}, more than the {credit} credit, so the seller would need to contribute more or you would cover the difference.

note_insurance_est: Homeowners insurance is estimated at {amt} a year for this home's price and age; it isn't a quote. Get a real quote during the inspection period.
note_insurance_given: Homeowners insurance uses {amt} a year, the figure given for this home.

note_closing_given: Closing costs are {pct} of the price, as given.

note_closing_lender_others: ; the other columns use about {pct} of the price{prepaids}{taxes}
note_credit_limits: A seller credit can only pay actual closing costs, prepaid items and escrows; any part above those costs is lost, and it can never be taken as cash. Seller-contribution limits: conventional 3% of price below 10% down, 6% at 10–25% down, 9% at 25% or more; FHA 6%; VA 4% in concessions plus normal closing costs. Confirm with your lender.
note_seller_cost: The seller doesn't net exactly the same at each split: each extra $10,000 of price also costs them about {amt} in {what}, plus their listing fee's share.
note_seller_cost_fee: The seller doesn't net exactly the same at each split: each extra $10,000 of price also costs them their listing fee's share.
note_cash: Cash available for the down payment and closing: about {cash}.
note_bb: The buyer's broker agreement is {agreement} of the price and the seller pays {seller}, so the difference counts in cash to close.
note_tax_rate: No millage for this area yet: the tax is estimated at about {pct} of the price. Confirm it with the property appraiser.
note_tax_assessed: Tax estimates assume the county values the home at the purchase price; it often values homes somewhat lower, so treat them as the high end. Flat assessments (garbage and other non-ad valorem charges) aren't included.
note_tax_portability: Portability isn't included: a buyer leaving a homestead in this state may carry part of its capped difference, which can lower the first bills (ask the property appraiser).
note_tax_which_higher: The parcel's taxing district isn't confirmed: the payment uses the {short} bill, the higher of the two, until it is.
note_tax_which: The parcel's taxing district isn't confirmed: the payment uses the {short} bill until it is.
